Hi. I think I found a bug in Lean. There is a function "UInt32.ofNatTruncate" in standard library, which clamps to "UInt32.maxValue" in case of overflow (and other similar functions.) But its name may be wrong, because, as well as I understand, the word "truncate" usually used in programming in different sense, i. e. "truncate" means truncating bits, which is totally different thing. (I'm not a native English speaker, so I'm not totally sure.)

Also, there is function USize.neg (a : USize) : USize. I think it (and similar functions) should be removed. There is little sense in negating unsigned number. If a user really wants to (for some reason) negate unsigned number, they can just write 0 - x

For the negation of uints: we like to have that uints form a commutative ring (also for the benefit of grind) which requires negation (see also lean4#7487). I agree though that "truncate" is a bit ambiguous and "clamp" would probably be more obvious.
Thank you for bringing up the naming issue, I renamed the function to UInt32.ofNatClamp in lean4#13627, to be included in Lean 4.31.0
Julia Markus Himmel thank you!
